note: How WPDS realizes the abstract language in ../../../patterns/index.json. Entries are keyed by `pattern`: an abstract id (`confirm`), a variant (`choose.segmented`) or a part (`navigate-hierarchy#descend`). `canonical`, `import`, `signature`, `instead_of` and `instead_of_signature` keep their meaning from version 1 and `signature` keeps the four-node floor; matching is containment, raw elements are transparent, `|` names alternative spellings. `detector` says how an entry is checked: `signature` (tree containment), `import` (the file imports `canonical`; nothing else to check), `declared` (documentation only until a declaration tag exists), or a rule object (a named AST rule the engine ships, parameterised here so the engine names no component). An entry under `parts` is loaded as `id#part` and inherits `canonical`/`import` unless it sets `canonical` to null explicitly; `rendered_signature` is a second shape under the same id. `canonical` is the name the code binds — a dotted part name is cut to its root on load. `verify: true` marks a component name taken from the abstract layer rather than checked against source; the generated table says so. Status gates (`experimental`, `locked`) come from components/index.json, not from here. The reach-for table in patterns.md is generated from this file and the abstract one: run `npm run patterns-doc` in engine/ after editing either.

detectors.signature: Tree containment against `signature`, four nodes or more. Extra children are fine; a registered child may sit anywhere beneath the root.
detectors.import: Satisfied when the file imports `canonical`; the tree is not inspected. For patterns whose whole implementation is one component.
detectors.declared: Checked only where the file declares the pattern (a `@pattern` tag); the declaration is compared to `canonical` and `signature`. No node floor, so a two-button bar is checkable once it is declared.
detectors.rule: A named AST rule that reads more than the component tree — option counts, button labels, event handlers. Listed under `rules`; each is a proposal until it ships.

rules.few-static-options: Shipped. A component in `components` whose `prop` is a static array literal (inline, or a same-file `const`) of `min`..`max` entries whose labels total at most `maxLabelChars` characters — the length stands in for the `fit: row` force, and a label the source does not state leaves the width unknown, which is not a finding. Reports the entry that carries it.
rules.confirm-pair: Shipped. A `container` whose only `button`s are exactly two with consent labels (`labels` regex, `__()`-wrapped or literal) and no form control (`controls` regex) inside. Reports the entry that carries it.
rules.judge: Shipped, behind `check --judge` only. Each element named in `components` is an instance of this entry's pattern. The forces that pattern's abstract `resolve` consults, where the vocabulary gives the force a `judge` block, are asked of TypeSafe one element at a time; `resolve` then runs in code, and a redirect reports `patterns/judged-redirect` (advisory, never in the hook or the baseline). An element carrying a prop in `unless` already realizes the target and is not asked, and neither is one with a spread, which might carry it.
rules.button-that-navigates: Specified. A Button whose onClick calls navigate(), history.push() or assigns window.location → the action-cluster destination redirect (Link). `judge` on action-cluster.bar reads the same thing from any handler; this deterministic form would let the hook see it.
rules.unconditional-optional-controls: Specified. A PanelBody rendering more than about six controls with no hasValue/onDeselect → field-group.progressive (ToolsPanel).
rules.hand-managed-selection: Specified. A run of Buttons each setting aria-selected or aria-pressed from state → browse-collection.selectable-list or choose.segmented by whether the values are records or options.

modal.note: Dialog (@wordpress/ui) is the eventual replacement; experimental per components/index.json — stay on Modal until that clears.

drawer.note: Experimental. Realize drawer-shaped tasks as Modal until it clears; declare the pattern as edit-record.drawer anyway so the migration is a find-and-replace later.

popover.note: Dropdown when the popover holds a control (a color editor); Popover for bare anchored content. Popover in @wordpress/ui is experimental.

menu.note: Menu in @wordpress/components is locked (system/locked-component). Outside Gutenberg core the shape is the same and the import is @wordpress/ui.

instead_of: A SelectControl with two to five options
A RadioControl for a set that fits on one row
A row of Buttons with isPressed and hand-managed exclusivity
realizations.note: `isDeselectable` plus an onChange that clears when the new value equals the old one is how 'no opinion' stays reachable without a 'None' option eating a slot.

Select (@wordpress/ui) is the eventual replacement; experimental. The trigger represents the current value — if it would represent a command, this is action-cluster.overflow (Menu); if a destination, navigate-hierarchy#descend.
Autocomplete (@wordpress/ui) covers the open-set case; experimental.

instead_of: A SelectControl of variation names
A RadioControl list of theme or preset names
Static thumbnails that are not the thing they preview
realizations.note: Each tile renders the real variation through a scoped style provider, marks the active one with aria-current, and puts the name in a Tooltip rather than under the tile. `Grid` is planned for deprecation — write the grid in CSS; the pattern is the live preview as the option, not that component.

instead_of: A bare RangeControl with the unit implied
A TextControl holding a CSS length as free text
A SelectControl of fixed sizes where the value is continuous
realizations.note: No canonical: Gutenberg composes this per site (FontSizeControl, SpacingSizesControl) rather than shipping one. Extract the project's own the first time it is built and fill `canonical` in. Bounds follow the unit: relative units get max 10 / step 0.1, absolute units get max 100 / step 1.

instead_of: A ColorPicker rendered inline for every color slot
A SelectControl of palette slug names
A reset button that is always visible whether or not anything is set
realizations.note: The signature is rooted in ToolsPanelItem because every color setting in a panel is also an item of field-group.progressive; the bare Dropdown > ZStack > ColorIndicator shape is under the floor on its own. Color and Gradient are Tabs inside the popover, not two controls. `ZStack` is planned for deprecation — the overlap is a CSS concern; the pattern is the rendered value.
In a data-bound form this is a DataForm field of type 'media' with Edit: MediaEdit — see edit-record.data-form. Outside one, MediaUpload from @wordpress/block-editor (verify).

instead_of: Label, control and help rebuilt per field with a hand-built Stack — Field.Root already handles the layout, association and a11y
Fieldset.Root for a group of controls sharing one legend, instead of Field.Root per control
realizations.note: The `*Control` components (TextControl, SelectControl, ToggleControl…) already are a field: label, help and error wired. Reach for Field only when composing a control that has no `*Control`, or when the fields are declared as data (edit-record.data-form), which never needs it.

instead_of: A PanelBody rendering all twelve possible controls at once
A stack of controls with no per-control reset
A hand-rolled 'Show advanced' toggle hiding half of them
realizations.note: Each item declares hasValue / onDeselect / isShownByDefault / panelId; the panel owns resetAll. A block settings screen orders it preview first, then one ToolsPanel per concern, Advanced last and collapsed.

instead_of: A stack of TextControls with a useState per field and a hand-written onChange each
Media pickers wired up individually instead of a field of type 'media'
A submit button doing what editEntityRecord already does per keystroke
realizations.note: The site editor's whole Identity pane is four field descriptors and a four-line form config; state is getEditedEntityRecord / editEntityRecord. The anti-shapes are deliberately rooted in a Modal or a Card: a bare Stack of three TextControls is the ordinary block-inspector panel, which edits attributes rather than an entity.

instead_of: Modal with an inline form and per-instance submit placement
realizations.note: No canonical: WPDS ships the container (see containers.modal), not the form dialog. Extract the project's own the first time a second screen needs it and fill `canonical` in. Dialog (@wordpress/ui) is the eventual container; experimental. Measured on 2110 Gutenberg files, this signature written with Stack alone missed nine real modals built with VStack/Flex; keep the alternation.
Drawer is experimental — see containers.drawer. Realize as Modal today; declare the variant so the finding can name Drawer the day the registry clears it.

instead_of: One-off panel layouts with bespoke headers
realizations.note: Not shipped. Extract the project's own the first time a second screen needs it and fill `canonical` in. A header row (title Text + a Button) and a body holding at least one field, both as the panel's own children: written with layout primitives, Text and Button alone, and matched at any depth, this signature fired on whole screens whose outer Stack held some row with a label and a button somewhere.

instead_of: A flow editor whose layout re-runs on every edit, so an arrangement the author made is gone by the next keystroke
Endpoints that can be grabbed and dropped and silently spring back, because nothing asked the model whether the move was allowed
realizations.note: Not shipped: WPDS has no canvas, and nothing here draws an edge. A project that needs one extracts it and fills `canonical` in — including the routing, which is a decision about every line at once and cannot be left to each edge. The card's own fields stay in edit-record.inspector beside it.

instead_of: div.actions with hand-set margins
Buttons spaced with margin-right
realizations.note: Stack direction=row, gap, primary last. Stack(Button, Button) is a true description and matches half a codebase, so it is checkable only when declared; layout/margin-on-child catches the usual defect regardless.

instead_of: A Stack of Buttons with a Divider between the groups — it looks the same and has no roving focus, so every control is a tab stop
realizations.note: A plain Button inside a Toolbar is the same defect one level down: it drops out of the roving-focus order. Verify Toolbar/ToolbarGroup/ToolbarButton status in components/index.json before relying on this entry.

instead_of: Rename and Delete rendered as two secondary Buttons in a header
A destructive Button sitting in the primary action row
realizations.note: The menu item opens a confirm dialog; it never destroys anything itself. Items that would do nothing are dropped from the menu rather than disabled. See containers.menu for the locked/experimental split.

instead_of: A hand-built Modal + Stack + Button pair reimplementing confirm/cancel — ConfirmDialog already does this, controlled or uncontrolled
window.confirm()
realizations.note: AlertDialog (@wordpress/ui) is the eventual replacement; experimental. The signature also matches edit-record.dialog — that is why the rule reads the button labels and checks for the absence of form controls, and why a declaration settles it outright.

stack.note: Screens are declared flat with path strings ('/typography/font-sizes/:origin/:slug'), never nested as JSX. The site editor syncs an outer router to Navigator rather than letting the component own its position.

descend.note: `Navigator.Button as={Item}` inside ItemGroup. When the abstract force `representation` is rendered, the row's leading element is the value: the palette row stacks five ColorIndicators, the typography row renders 'Aa' in the live face and color, the font row sets the family name in its own face. `rendered_signature` is the same part with that force applied, not a second pattern.

sub-screen-header.note: No canonical: the header is rebuilt per project; extract it. Navigator.BackButton handles the common case; pass an explicit onBack only when the path carries a selection ('/revisions/12') rather than a sub-screen, where popping one segment would land nowhere.

instead_of: Tabs standing in for hierarchy — tabs are for siblings, not for parent and child
One long scrolling panel holding every control for every level
A SelectControl that swaps which panel is rendered
A column of Buttons standing in for navigation
Anchors styled to look like list rows
A bare heading plus a Button with an arrow icon, rebuilt per sub-screen
A breadcrumb trail inside a panel that is already one screen deep
A SelectControl that swaps its body
Several Modals for what is one task with several sources
realizations.note: Inside a Modal this is screen.overlay: the modal supplies the footer, the tabs switch the body, and a tab's own content can be a navigate-hierarchy (the font library installs from a tab and edits a family on a sub-screen of it).

instead_of: Custom filter/search/action clusters per list
toolbar.note: DataViews owns search, filters and bulk actions when the list is a DataViews. This shape is only correct above a collection that is not one.

instead_of: A SelectControl sitting beside the search field
A row of filter chips built from Buttons with isPressed
toolbar.filter.note: The abstract part is one `choose` per filter dimension; WPDS realizes it compactly as a radio menu behind an icon beside the search field. Announce the result count with speak() so a filter change is perceivable without sight of the list.

instead_of: A stack of Buttons with aria-selected managed by hand
A RadioControl standing in for a list of records
A DataViews table whose only action is 'select'
realizations.note: role="listbox" on the Composite, role="option" plus aria-selected on each item, render={<div/>} so the item is not also a button.

instead_of: A grid of static images standing in for live output
A list of names with the rendering left to the reader's imagination
Sections built from headings with no grouping semantics
realizations.note: Examples render inside an iframe carrying the real styles, wrapped in Disabled so nothing in a preview is focusable.

instead_of: An editable table of presets with inline delete buttons
A repeater of TextControl + NumberControl rows
One flat list that hides which origin a preset came from
realizations.note: Not shipped; the site editor's preset groups are the reference. Origin is the grouping and decides what is offered: theme and default groups get Reset (only while they differ from base), custom gets Add, Rename and Delete. Each row is navigate-hierarchy#descend; the overflow is action-cluster.overflow.

instead_of: A centred div (or hand-built Stack + Text + Button) with a paragraph and a button
Individually placed Notice components with local margins — NoticeList already takes notices + onRemove
realizations.note: Stack(Notice) is under the floor; the import is the check. Notice (@wordpress/ui) compound is experimental — do not swap preemptively.

instead_of: A hand-managed array of messages in component state, rendered into a fixed-position Stack
A confirm dialog on a reversible action
realizations.note: Raise through the notices store (createNotice with type 'snackbar' and an undo action); mount the list once. Verify SnackbarList's status before relying on this entry.
Spinner in @wordpress/components is legacy; the @wordpress/ui one is recommended.

instead_of: A styled div with a border/shadow rebuilt per surface

realizations.note: Text at a heading variant with render supplying the element, then a Stack. Nothing to import; nothing to check beyond the declaration and typography/raw-element.

instead_of: An ad-hoc row Stack + heading Text + buttons rebuilt per screen
header.note: Page ships this: title, headingLevel, optional breadcrumbs and icon, an `actions` slot, and hasPadding for the body. The site editor's Styles and Identity panes are both <Page title actions> with no hand-built header. The title stack and the actions stack are pinned (`>`) to the header row itself: matched at any depth, a screen's outer Stack holding two Texts in one place and a Button in another read as a hand-built page header.

realizations.note: The former modal-with-tabs: a container plus switch-view.tabs, not a pattern of its own. No canonical — the composition is not shipped; the container is Modal and the tabs are switch-view.tabs.
The header is navigate-hierarchy#sub-screen-header; the body is a leaf. Declare it; the hierarchy entry carries the checks.
